Additionally, the sewer hydraulic model will be updated and calibrated using flow data collected by monitoring devices. Other tasks will include assessments of the force mains and the suction and discharge pipes at the three lift stations.  The Sewer Master Plan will become the District’s new planning document describing improvement needs and expenditures for the next 20 years.

Please do not flush wet wipes, paper towels, feminine products or trash of any kind.   • SJSU will draft an administrative procedure to detail after hours protocols regarding how to respond to and who to call during a sewer overflow emergency.  This will help to streamline the response strategy, hasten repair and reduce/eliminate discharge volume. • At least once per year SJSU will jet and scope the lines, including laterals, to ensure that they remain clear and flowing.   • SJSU will stage a jetter at south campus during game days. FIRST_ROW_NAME_ADDRESS: 001,    , Ventura, CA
ACTIONS_TAKEN_TO_ADDRESS_DEFICIENCIES: The February 2024 sewer spill revealed some system deficiencies. These pipe segments were inspected in 2022, but the severity of these deficiencies was not apparent during the CCTV inspection performed at that time. Immediately after the spill, OVSD replaced the damaged asbestos cement pipe (ACP) segment that caused the SSO with PVC pipe. OVSD inspected all ACP near the spill location. OVSD determined the two segments immediately upstream of the spill pipe segment were in a deteriorated condition. OVSD rehabilitated those segments with cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) on an emergency basis. OVSD determined that the ACP downstream of OVSD’s Meiners Oaks Siphon (MO Siphon) were in worse condition than the pipelines upstream of the MO Siphon tie-in, likely due to turbulent siphon flows and H2S gas exposure. OVSD went out to public bid on a CIPP rehabilitation of 5,070 LF of trunk sewer beginning at the downstream tie-in of the MO Siphon. 5,070 LF of CIPP rehabilitation was completed 12/2024.
